title: How much more than one lakh is Chintamani now?
description: A question from the book gives the estimated population of Chintamani in twenty twenty four and asks how much more it is than one lakh. The video finds the gap by taking the smaller number from the larger, and checks it by adding back.
teaching_notes: One idea: how much more means the gap above a number, found by taking the smaller number from the larger. Ask the class to add the gap back to one lakh and see whether the population returns. Watch for students who write the gap with a missing zero or subtract in the wrong order.

video_script.why: The child knows one lakh is 1,00,000 and can find a gap by subtracting.
video_script.substitution: To find how much more, take the smaller number away from the larger one.
video_script.anchor: The estimated population of Chintamani in twenty twenty four is one lakh six thousand: how much more than one lakh is that?
video_script.payoff_line: One lakh six thousand is six thousand more than one lakh

final_answer.spoken: six thousand more than one lakh

video_script.design: One idea: how much more means the gap above a number. The method of the rice question is reused: compare with one lakh by subtracting. The anchor stays all video; the working band builds in the idea part; no hard clear.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, count up in two hops. From one lakh to one lakh five thousand is five thousand.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>From one lakh five thousand to one lakh six thousand is one thousand.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, check by putting the hops back in the question. One lakh, plus five thousand, plus one thousand.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>That lands exactly on one lakh six thousand, so the hops are right.
